question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides equal protection of the laws and equality before the law?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 14**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 14 deals with The Right to Equality.
 
• Article 14:
 
 
• ​Articles 14-18 deal with the Right to Equality.
 
• Equality before the law.
 
• The state shall not deny to any person equality before the law or equal protection of the law within the territory of India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 30**

 
 
• **​**Minorities are granted the freedom to create and run their educational institutions. Also known as the "Charter of Education Rights," Article 30.
 
• Article 30(1)
 
 
• States that every linguistic and religious minority has the freedom to create and run educational institutions of their choosing.
 
 
 
• Article 30(2)
 
 
• Prohibits the State from discriminating against any educational institution because it is run by a minority, regardless of religion or language, while providing funding to educational institutions.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Article 42**
 
 
• Article 42 insists that the State should ensure just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief.
 
• Article 42 of the Constitution is a non-government organization operating in the sphere of protection of human rights facilitating the protection of civic and political rights and freedoms, as well as the protection of other fundamental rights recognized by international law.
 
• **Harmonization of state policy and national legislation with international standards.**
 
 
 
• ​**Article 60:**
 
 
• ​Article 60 of the Indian constitution talks about the** Oath or affirmation by the President.**
 
• It states that** “Every President and every person acting as President or discharging the functions of the President shall, before entering upon his office, make and subscribe in the presence of the Chief Justice of India or, in his absence, the senior most Judge of the Supreme Court available.”**
